correctness.rationale: For a genuine (n,b) reverse multiple, b≥3, 2≤n<b, nonzero endpoint digits, the grade-school recurrence b c_(j+1)=n d_(k−j)+c_j−d_j with c_0=c_(k+1)=0 ensures 0≤c_j≤n−1. Eliminating paired reversed digits gives (n²−1)d_j=nb c_(k−j+1)−n c_(k−j)+b c_(j+1)−c_j. At j=k this yields (n²−1)d_k=nb c_1−c_k>0, forcing c_1>0. If c_k=c_(k−1)=0, the j=0,1 identities force D=n²−1 to divide b c_1 and b c_2−c_1. Multiplying the first by c_2 and second by c_1 and subtracting yields D|c_1²; but 0<c_1²≤(n−1)²<D, contradiction. In an outer-zero padded contiguous carry string, c_0=0 and c_1>0 force exactly one lower zero; two-highest-zero exclusion allows at most one upper zero. Only necessary shapes (d_m..d_0,0) and (0,d_m..d_0,0) survive, not asserted realizable. Independently checked modular obstruction for n=2..39, n<b≤59; this supplements exact universal inequality, not a surrogate for proof. Scope excludes internal digit insertions and other derived constructions.

value.rationale: The source and literature motivate a concrete open-ended classification of derived palintiple carry encodings. The new D|c_1² boundary obstruction is a universal structural lemma, ruling out all longer exterior zero-padding of an intact source carry word. Though elementary and deliberately narrow, it gives a principled impossibility boundary for the precisely defined family without claiming to resolve arbitrary third/fourth derivations.
